review_notes: I read the whole target file. I compared it with FullLocalDegree.lean, LocalGlobal/AbsoluteGaloisGroup.lean and Galois/Restriction.lean. Nothing was compiled, so the proposed rewrites are untested. The main uncertainty in finding 1 is the elaboration detail of matching `L.val.restrictNormalHom` with `AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L`, using the existing simp lemma `IntermediateField.restrictNormalHom_val`. In finding 2 the repeated block is short and is the weaker case. Within the file itself, the three theorems do not share reasoning with each other, so the duplication is with existing library lemmas. Neither of those lemma files imports the target, so no import cycle arises.

findings.problem: The body re-proves, with `ι` specialised to the inclusion `L → Kˢ`, the existing lemma `AlgHom.exists_stabilizer_le_range_restrictNormalHom_comp_absoluteGaloisGroupMap`. The repeated steps are: lift the embedding `κ : L_w → K_vˢ` with `IsSepClosed.lift`; form `L → L_w → K_vˢ`; extend it to `τ : Kˢ → K_vˢ` with `surjective_domRestrict_of_isSeparable`; derive `hτ_apply`; lift `decompositionHom v w σ` with `restrictNormalHom_surjective`; then run the same `absoluteGaloisGroupMap_commutes` / `restrictNormalHom_commutes` / `decompositionHom_algebraMap` calc and finish with `τ.injective`. The last 20 lines are a hand-written copy of that chase. Any change to the decomposition-group lifting argument now has to be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change: Keep the first part of the proof (`NumberField L`, then `obtain ⟨v, w, hw⟩ := exists_stabilizer_eq_top_of_finrank_prime hL`, then `LiesOver`). Then call `obtain ⟨τ, hτ⟩ := L.val.exists_stabilizer_le_range_restrictNormalHom_comp_absoluteGaloisGroupMap (v := v) w.1`. Here `ι = L.val : L →ₐ[K] SeparableClosure K`, and `Normal K L` and `IsGalois K L` come from the existing instances. Finish with `refine ⟨v, τ, fun σ ↦ ?_⟩` and `obtain ⟨g, hg⟩ := hτ (hw ▸ Subgroup.mem_top σ)`, so that `hg : (L.val.restrictNormalHom.comp (absoluteGaloisGroupMap τ)) g = σ`. Close with `⟨g, by simpa using hg⟩`, using the existing simp lemma `IntermediateField.restrictNormalHom_val : L.val.restrictNormalHom = AlgEquiv.restrictNormalHom L` (Galois/Restriction.lean). The only new import is `TauCeti.NumberTheory.NumberField.LocalGlobal.AbsoluteGaloisGroup`. It already imports the same `AbsoluteGaloisGroup.Map` and `DecompositionGroup` modules as the target, and it does not import the target, so no cycle arises. This is how `FullLocalDegree.lean` already uses the lemma, via `E.val.exists_stabilizer_le_range_restrictNormalHom_comp_absoluteGaloisGroupMap`.
findings.benefit: This removes about 30 lines of non-trivial local-field and Galois-lifting reasoning. The decomposition-group-to-`G_{K_v}` lifting then lives in one lemma instead of two. This theorem becomes a short deduction from `exists_stabilizer_eq_top_of_finrank_prime`, and its mathematical content (a full decomposition group gives a surjection) is visible at a glance.

findings.excerpt: let _ : IsCyclic Gal(L/K) := isCyclic_of_prime_card (p := Nat.card Gal(L/K)) rfl
findings.problem: This proof repeats the argument of `exists_notMem_forall_stabilizer_eq_top_of_finrank_prime`. Both set up `Fact (Nat.card Gal(L/K)).Prime` and `IsCyclic`, and both argue by contradiction through `finrank_eq_one_of_stabilizer_eq_bot`. Both use `Subgroup.eq_bot_or_eq_top_of_prime_card` to turn 'not ⊤' into '⊥'. The target version is only the weaker `S = ∅` case. It even adds an unused-looking `IsMulCommutative` instance and an extra `under_surjective` step.
findings.proposed_change: Derive the target from the stronger existing lemma. Apply `exists_notMem_forall_stabilizer_eq_top_of_finrank_prime hL ∅` to get `v` with `hv : ∀ w, stabilizer … = ⊤`. Then take `w` from `HeightOneSpectrum.under_surjective (𝓞 K) (𝓞 L) v` (the existing lines 77–79) and finish with `⟨v, w, hv w⟩`. This requires importing `TauCeti.NumberTheory.ClassFieldTheory.Global.FullLocalDegree`, which does not depend on the target.
findings.benefit: The cyclic-group and prime-order bookkeeping and the contradiction argument then exist once. The prime-degree decomposition lemma is stated and maintained in a single place.
